01
From leadership

Inside Centricity: A word from our CEO

A word from Shakeel Abdul,Shakeel Abdulour Chief Executive Officer

Welcome to the first issue of our network newsletter. Since I joined Centricity in March, many of you have told me you want to know more about what’s happening beyond your own site or team. Starting with this issue, we’ll share news from across our sites and teams, and where we’re investing next.

The sponsors I’ve met this year have been asking us how we operate as a network. Many are working with fewer partners and placing more of their portfolios with networks instead of choosing sites study by study.

At Centricity, we are already a preferred partner to the world’s largest pharma companies and CROs. To protect that position, we believe strongly in being the best at serving our three customers: sponsors, PIs and patients. Sponsors place studies where investigators are engaged and patients enroll and stay. Investigators stay with us when we bring them the right studies and the support to run them well. And patients often come to us through doctors they already trust.

Q3 was our best quarter for enrollment since the start of 2025, with record enrollments in the U.S. and our strongest bookings in Canada in two years. We set a stretch forecast and beat it. More of the patients we screened went on to enroll, up from about half to more than 60%, which shows sponsors we are getting better at finding the right patients. Study awards rose by two thirds compared with Q3 last year, and we’ve added 36 new team members across the network since spring.

We are profitable and generate enough cash to fund our own growth. That lets us build capacity ahead of study awards, so we can compete on speed of enrollment and patient experience. Here is where we’re investing:

  • Our PIs. We’ve completed more feasibilities this year than in all of 2025, and we’re asking sponsors to share their pipelines 12 to 18 months out. We anticipate high growth in cardiovascular, renal and metabolic (CVRM) studies and in immunology and inflammation (I&I). We’re also investing in new compensation models that reward PIs for patients they identify from their own practices, and building out sub investigators to support them.
  • Patient recruitment. We’re rolling out a recruitment platform across every site, built to enroll patients faster. It texts and books qualified patients automatically, screens each one for multiple studies, and shows us which sources and campaigns lead to randomizations. It also gives us a better way to reach patients who have been in our studies before.
  • Speed to first patient. We’re shortening the time from contract to first patient across the network, while still negotiating fair budgets for our sites.
  • Pay tied to results. More pay is moving into incentives tied to screenings and randomizations, so the people doing the work share directly in what the network achieves.

Growing the network

The CRE program

CRE connects Centricity with providers outside our research sites. A provider signs on, then connects patients from their own practice into studies they would be a fit for.

Of the 84 active providers, 35 connected at least one patient this year, into 63 different studies. Canada joined CRE in late 2025, so part of the jump against last year is a second country coming online.

07
From the CMOFrom leadership

Joseph on the year aheadThe year ahead: A word from our CMO

Joseph SurberChief Medical Officer

As we head toward 2027, one of the things I’m most excited about is the opportunity to deepen provider engagement across Centricity and within the communities we serve.

We have an incredible group of PIs, Sub-Investigators, community providers and site teams across the organization. Our focus is on creating more opportunities for them to participate in research, making it easier to identify and give appropriate patients access to clinical trials, and continuing to bring studies into our sites that make sense for the communities we serve.

Programs like CRE are already helping us engage providers beyond the walls of our research sites, while we continue to strengthen our investigator network and build relationships in new communities. We are also working to better recognize and reward the investigators who actively contribute to the success of our studies. The more connected and engaged our investigators, providers, site teams and communities become, the better we will be at enrolling studies and, more importantly, giving patients access to research that may help shape the future of medicine.

Clinical research gives us the opportunity not only to improve how medicine is practiced today, but to help develop the treatments that will change how it is practiced tomorrow. That’s what makes this work exciting, and why I believe Centricity has an incredible opportunity ahead.

There is plenty of work to do, but I’m genuinely excited about what we can accomplish together in 2027.

Beyond our network

What we heard at SCRS

SCRSGlobal Site Solutions Summit · Orlando · October 15 to 18

Sponsors are moving from picking sites study by study to longer term partnerships based on data. Choosing the right site is the start. What keeps the partnership working is pipeline visibility and a proven record up front, then communication throughout.

42%
of sites citecontract and budget negotiation with sponsors as the top cause of delay, unchanged
$75K to $100K
what a single site that never enrollscosts a sponsor in direct operational expense
12 to 18 months
of pipeline visibilitygiven to strategic sites, early enough to plan around

Fewer sites reported sponsor pauses (37%), supply delays (30%) and protocol amendments (27%). Three of the four rank where they did the last time the question was asked.

What it means for your site
01Where the work comes from

Partner networks now make 67% of AstraZeneca’s site picks, up from 10% at launch. The target is 80%. Strategic sites also get 12 to 18 months of pipeline visibility.

02What gets you picked

Startup time, recruitment speed, retention, data timeliness, query turnaround. Your record counts, not your feasibility form. AstraZeneca is building capability profiles so the same basics are not asked twice.

03What happens if you do not start

If nothing is screened 30 days after activation, the sponsor calls to ask why. First screening is generally expected within 15 to 30 days.

04What to say when it is not a fit

Say so. An honest estimate protects the next opportunity. An optimistic one falls apart at screening.

05What keeps the relationship

Sponsors named communication as the main driver of site success. Flag enrollment barriers early and keep clear escalation paths between site, CRA and study team. Staff turnover at the CRO is what most often breaks them.

Source
  • SCRSGlobal Site Solutions Summit 2026 · study delays, site selection, feasibility and partnership sessions
